lab04-s000.title: Before You Begin
lab04-s000.markdown:
**Estimated time:** 25 minutes
**What you will create:** A statistical forecast based on the past 24 months of actuals, a rolling forecast whose horizon extends as periods close, and a writeback configuration that saves planning data to Fabric SQL. ---

lab04-s001.title: The Story So Far
lab04-s001.markdown:
The plan is complete. But when January closes, actuals are **$1.92M** against a forecast of **$2.09M**. With the old Excel workbook, discovering this gap took 11 days, followed by a week of work by three people to revise the forecast.

In this module, you will create a forecast that can be updated as actuals are finalized and write the results back to Fabric SQL. This makes planning data available to Power BI, semantic models, and data agents too.

This module is about making the plan useful across the organization, not just within finance.

> [!NOTE]
> Values dependent on data, periods, and settings, such as forecast amounts and writeback row counts, are output examples, not fixed pass criteria. Check the values shown in your environment, the forecast assumptions, and the destination.

---

lab04-s002.title: Part 1: Create a Forecast Sheet
lab04-s002.markdown:
1. On the **Home** ribbon, select **New Planning Sheet**. If prompted to save when switching, use **Save and Proceed** to save the current edits. Set the name to `Forecast` and select **Create**.

   ![New Planning Sheet just before creation, with Forecast entered in Name](../assets/screenshots/lab04/01-forecast-create.png)

   After creation, **Forecast** is added to Explorer and becomes the selected sheet. No data has been assigned yet.

   ![Example Forecast sheet added to Explorer after creation](../assets/screenshots/lab04/02-forecast-created.png)

2. Arrange the fields as follows:

   | Placement | Value | Source table |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Rows** | *Category* → *Sub Category* | *Product* |
   | **Columns** | *Year*, *Quarter*, *Month Short* | *Date* |
   | **Values** | *Gross Revenue* | *Measures Table* |

   Expand **Product** in the **Data** pane and place **Category → Sub Category**, in that order, in **Rows** under **Fields**. Next, place **Year → Quarter → Month Short** from **Date** in **Columns**, and **Gross Revenue** from **Measures Table** in **Values**. Check the source table to avoid confusing it with another measure of the same name.

   ![Category from Product added to Rows, with Processing Data displayed](../assets/screenshots/lab04/03-category-assigned.png)

   ![Rows ordered Category, Sub Category, with Values not yet configured](../assets/screenshots/lab04/04-rows-assigned.png)

   ![Year from Date placed in Columns, before adding Quarter, Month Short, and Gross Revenue](../assets/screenshots/lab04/05-year-assigned.png)

   Next, add **Quarter** and **Month Short** to Columns, then finally add **Gross Revenue**, which is not restricted to a particular year, to Values.

   ![Year and Quarter placed in Columns, with Processing Data displayed](../assets/screenshots/lab04/06-quarter-assigned.png)

   ![All three Columns fields ordered Year, Quarter, Month Short](../assets/screenshots/lab04/07-columns-assigned.png)

   ![Gross Revenue from Measures Table placed in Values, with 2025 Gross Revenue unselected](../assets/screenshots/lab04/08-gross-revenue-assigned.png)

   Wait for **Processing Data** to disappear, then confirm two fields in Rows, three in Columns, and Gross Revenue in Values. With the same data, an example before filtering shows four columns for 2023–2026, All-row values of **23.28 / 24.57 / 25.87 / 26.56M**, respectively, and a footer of **Rows: 21 / Columns: 4**. These are rounded displays of actuals, not forecast results. Values and column counts depend on the data.

> [!NOTE]
> This module uses *Gross Revenue*, **not restricted to a particular year**, rather than *2025 Gross Revenue*. Statistical forecasting needs multiple years of history, whereas a measure restricted to 2025 exposes only one year. Modules 01 and 03 used year-specific measures for single-year planning; this module is different.

3. Open the panel using the **Filter** icon at the far right. Among the field cards under **Page level**, expand **Year** and check **2024** and **2025** under **Basic**.

   ![Example before filtering: grid, six fields, and Page level filter cards](../assets/screenshots/lab04/09-filter-panel-initial.png)

   ![Initial Year state is (All), showing all four years without filtering even though individual year checkboxes are empty](../assets/screenshots/lab04/10-year-filter-all.png)

   **Pay attention to the initial state.** Even if all checkboxes are empty, **Year is (All)** displays every year. Rather than unchecking 2023 and 2026, **check the years you want: 2024 / 2025**. After selecting, verify that both the checkmarks and the displayed columns include only 2024 and 2025.

   **Display example:** With the condition **Year is '2024, 2025'**, 2024 / 2025 checked, and 2023 / 2026 unchecked, the grid shows two columns: 2024 All **24.57M** and 2025 All **25.87M**. The footer is **Rows: 21 / Columns: 2**. Actual values and row and column counts depend on the data.

   ![Example with 2024 and 2025 checked, showing the Year condition and two years of actuals](../assets/screenshots/lab04/11-year-filter-2024-2025.png)

   Select **Save** at the top right and wait for saving to complete. Then check the fields, year filter, and displayed columns. To verify retention after saving, reload the browser as needed and check the same settings.

   ![Example after saving: 2024 and 2025 condition, two years of actuals, and six fields](../assets/screenshots/lab04/12-filtered-history-saved.png)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Apply this filter **before** creating the forecast measure. The statistical model reads historical data within the target scope. Filtering afterward would mean creating a forecast without using the intended history.

4. On the **Planning** ribbon, select **Totals**. Open the **Column Subtotal** dropdown and change it to **Left**. Do not confuse it with the separate **Column Grand Total** setting.

   ![Example Totals menu with Off selected for Column Subtotal](../assets/screenshots/lab04/13-subtotal-off-menu.png)

   ![Selecting Left from the Column Subtotal options Left, Right, and Off](../assets/screenshots/lab04/14-subtotal-left-option.png)

   ![Example with Column Subtotal set to Left and Year collapsed](../assets/screenshots/lab04/15-subtotal-left-set.png)

> [!NOTE]
> It is fine if nothing looks different yet. Subtotals aggregate **visible child members** in the hierarchy. While columns are collapsed at Year, the children to aggregate are not visible; each Year column itself already represents an aggregate. Expanding a year with `>` displays a subtotal column alongside its quarters. Enabling it now makes it available when needed.

lab04-s003.title: Part 2: Define a Forecast Measure
lab04-s003.markdown:
1. For more screen space, collapse **Fields / Data / Filter**. Select **Forecast** on the **Model** ribbon to open **Insert Forecast Measures**. The wizard has three stages: **Basic → Closed Periods → Open Periods**.

   ![Forecast sheet showing 2024 and 2025 actuals with the Model ribbon open](../assets/screenshots/lab04/16-model-ribbon-filtered.png)

2. In **Basic**, enter `Forecast` for **Measure Name**. Check **Forecast Period** and, if needed, set it to `Jan 2026 - Dec 2026`. Leave **Multi Dimension Allocation: Off** and select **Next**. This is before the final save; the forecast measure has not yet finished being created.

   ![Insert Forecast Measures Basic settings: Measure Name Forecast, Jan 2026 - Dec 2026, and Multi Dimension Allocation Off](../assets/screenshots/lab04/17-forecast-basic-settings.png)
3. In **Closed Periods**, select **Link to Measure**, confirm **Source Measure: Gross Revenue**, and select **Next**.

   ![Example Closed Periods settings: Link to Measure and Source Measure Gross Revenue](../assets/screenshots/lab04/18-forecast-closed-settings.png)

4. In **Open Periods**, set **Data Input** and **Default Value: None**. Do not add the optional **Pre-fill Open periods**. Select **Save** once and wait for the wizard to close and the Forecast columns to be created.

   ![Example Open Periods settings: Data Input, Default Value None, and no pre-fill](../assets/screenshots/lab04/19-forecast-open-settings.png)

This distinction is the basis of rolling forecasts. **Closed periods** automatically reference actuals, while **open periods** allow planning values to be entered. As time passes, moving each month from open to closed updates the forecast to incorporate actuals.

**Check the creation result.** Confirm that the sheet title shows **Gross Revenue, Forecast** and that a column group for the forecast period and **Forecast** columns have been added. If the year filter includes only 2024 and 2025, 2026 shows **Forecast only**, with blank values. This is not a generated statistical forecast.

![After Forecast creation, 2024 and 2025 actuals and Forecast show the same annual amounts, while 2026 Forecast is blank](../assets/screenshots/lab04/20-forecast-created-result.png)

| Year | Value displayed in Forecast | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 2024 | All row displays **24.57M**, the same as Gross Revenue | Closed period referencing actuals through Link to Measure |
| 2025 | All row displays **25.87M**, the same as Gross Revenue | Same as above |
| 2026 | **Blank** | Open period with no default input value |

Confirm that Forecast is locked for closed periods and references actuals. Rounded annual displays alone cannot reconcile every digit of every month's internally stored values. No statistical forecast has been generated at this point. Later steps save forecast values and verify their retention after reloading.

If 2024 or 2025 Forecast differs from actuals, check **Closed Periods: Source Measure**. If 2026 is not blank, check **Open Periods: Default Value / Pre-fill**.

lab04-s004.title: Part 3: Generate a Statistical Forecast
lab04-s004.markdown:
1. Select the **All**-row cell in **2026 Forecast**. It is fine for it to be blank. You will populate it with a statistical forecast.

   With years collapsed, single-click the 2026 Forecast annual cell and confirm that the selection border appears. You do not need to fill the blank with zero or confirm a value edit.

   ![Years collapsed, with the blank All-row 2026 Forecast annual cell selected](../assets/screenshots/lab04/21-forecast-2026-selected.png)

> [!TIP]
> Leave the column hierarchy collapsed at Year. With 2026 collapsed, this single cell represents the annual value, making it appropriate as the forecast target. Microsoft's tutorial calls it the “2026 Forecast subtotal,” but a separate subtotal column does not appear until the year is expanded to quarters.

2. Select **Predict** on the **Model** ribbon. The **Predict** panel opens on the right.
3. At the top of the panel, confirm **Row Selected** is `GrandTotal` and **Measure Selected** is `Forecast`. Select the lock icon in each field to pin the selection. This prevents the forecast target from changing when you click another cell in the sheet.
4. Under **Set Period Range**, confirm **Historic Data Range** is `Jan 2024 - Dec 2025` and **Forecast Date Range** is `Jan 2026 - Dec 2026`. These are normally correct at this point because they are derived from the filter and forecast period configured earlier.

   Verify **GrandTotal / Forecast** and lock both fields. Confirm that the button labels change to **Unlock**. If the historical or forecast periods differ from the intended ranges, correct them here.

   ![Example Predict settings: GrandTotal / Forecast, historical and forecast periods, and initial profile](../assets/screenshots/lab04/22-predict-defaults-locked.png)
5. Under **Configure Forecast**, leave **Select Profile** as `Profile 1` and configure:

   | Setting | Value | Default |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Confidence (%)** | `90` | Already 90 |
   | **Growth Factor (%)** | `4` | **0, so you must change it** |
   | **Evaluation** | Bottom Up | Already Bottom Up |
   | **Round all negative values to zero** | No | Already No |

   Confidence and Growth Factor each provide a slider and numeric input. Entering the numbers directly is easier than dragging the sliders.

   Change **Growth Factor** from its initial **0** to **4** and verify **Profile 1 / Confidence 90 / Growth Factor 4 / Bottom Up / No**.

   ![Example settings: Growth Factor 4, Confidence 90, Bottom Up, and negative-value handling No](../assets/screenshots/lab04/23-predict-profile-settings.png)

<details>
<summary>What the settings mean</summary>

**Select Profile** selects a profile that stores confidence, growth factor, evaluation direction, negative-value handling, algorithm, and seasonality together. Use **More options (...)** to create, duplicate, delete, or reset profiles. A descriptive name lets you reproduce the same forecasting conditions later without relying on memory. One profile is sufficient for this lab.

**Confidence (%)** sets the forecast uncertainty interval based on the model and its assumptions. Increasing it normally widens the interval without changing the central forecast itself. Set it to 90 for this exercise. This does not mean “90% forecast accuracy,” nor does it guarantee that future actuals have a 90% probability of falling within the range or that the target will be achieved. Validation by forecasting a held-out portion of historical data and comparing with actual results, and checks for business plausibility, are separate requirements. The [official forecasting FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-forecasting/forecasting-faq) also explains that changing Confidence changes the width of uncertainty, not the center line.

**Growth Factor (%)** adds a business adjustment to the statistical forecast result. At 0%, the statistical forecast is used as is; at 4%, each forecast value is increased by 4% to reflect expected growth. A negative value reduces it. This lets planners incorporate judgment into a model that otherwise refers only to historical data.

**Evaluation** specifies the calculation direction. **Bottom Up** forecasts each detail row and rolls up, reflecting subcategory-specific patterns. **Top Down** forecasts the overall total and then allocates it downward.

**Round all negative values to zero** matters for metrics that should not be negative. Even if revenue cannot be negative, the statistical model may not recognize that constraint. A sharply declining series can produce a negative forecast. Set this to **No** in this exercise.

**Choose Algorithm** offers three options:

| Algorithm | Suitable data |
|---|---|
| **Trend Decomposition with MSTL** | Data with multiple overlapping cyclical patterns; decomposes it into components that are easier to model |
| **Exponential Smoothing** | Data with one clear seasonal cycle and a smooth trend; emphasizes recent values |
| **ARIMA** | Data where recent spikes, drops, or lagged movements provide forecasting clues |

</details>

6. Under **Choose Algorithm**, select **Trend Decomposition with MSTL**. Expand **Customize Algorithm** if collapsed, and turn on both **Year / Quarter** under **Set Seasonality**.

   ![Example with MSTL selected and both Year / Quarter enabled under Set Seasonality](../assets/screenshots/lab04/24-predict-seasonality-year-quarter.png)

7. Select **Run Forecast** once. Confirm that each month of the forecast period appears in **Forecast Table** with **Type: Forecast**, and that **Save Forecast** is available. You do not need to run again to inspect the result.

   ![Example Forecast Table showing 12 monthly forecast rows and Save Forecast](../assets/screenshots/lab04/25-statistical-forecast-preview.png)

   | Month | Example Forecast Table display |
   |---|---:|
   | Jan 2026 | 2091.951k |
   | Feb 2026 | 2114.444k |
   | Mar 2026 | 2208.407k |
   | Apr 2026 | 2243.381k |
   | May 2026 | 2291.780k |
   | Jun 2026 | 2434.714k |
   | Jul 2026 | 2484.113k |
   | Aug 2026 | 2400.480k |
   | Sep 2026 | 2288.689k |
   | Oct 2026 | 2290.802k |
   | Nov 2026 | 2421.308k |
   | Dec 2026 | 2724.496k |

   **k means 1,000.** The nominal total of the displayed values above is **27,994,565**, but this sums preview values rounded to three decimal places in k units. Distinguish it from full internal precision and the annual cell value after saving. This is an example output preview, not confirmation that the measure has been saved. Actual values depend on data and settings.

8. Check the preview target and periods, then select **Save Forecast**. In the confirmation screen, verify the measure and date range and select **Save**.

   Confirm **Select Measure: Forecast** and the target **Date Range**. Read the notice that existing values in the specified range will be overwritten, then select **Save** once.

   ![Example Save Forecast screen specifying Forecast and Jan 2026 - Dec 2026](../assets/screenshots/lab04/26-save-forecast-confirm-settings.png)

   After saving, confirm the Predict panel closes. In the display example, All-row 2026 Forecast was **27.99M**, and the annual cell's edit bar showed **27994564.7621**. Double-click the annual cell to read its value, then close with **Escape** without confirming a change. Actual values depend on data and settings.

   **Check retention after reloading.** Wait for **Save** at the top right of the Plan to complete, then reload the browser. Switch to **Editing**, select **Forecast** in Explorer, wait for the data, and confirm the forecast values are retained. The following are display examples.

   ![Example after reload: Forecast opened in Editing, with All-row 2026 Forecast at 27.99M](../assets/screenshots/lab04/27-forecast-reopened-result.png)

   ![Example annual edit bar after reload: 27994564.7621](../assets/screenshots/lab04/28-forecast-annual-editor.png)

   Monthly forecast displays are rounded, so their sum may differ from the annual value. Summing rounded monthly amounts does not indicate the precision of internal values or the annual cell after saving.

> [!NOTE]
> MSTL decomposes a time series into trend and multiple seasonal components. Harborlight is a consumer goods company with quarterly promotional cycles as well as an annual cycle, so both seasonalities are selected.

9. In **Filter → Year → Basic**, keep 2024 and 2025 selected and check **2026**. Although the 2026 Forecast column already exists, **Gross Revenue** appears only after you include 2026 in the year filter. Verify the 2024 / 2025 / 2026 checkmarks, close Fields / Data / Filter, and compare actual and forecast columns. Do not rerun the forecast.

   ![Example year filter with 2024, 2025, and 2026 selected](../assets/screenshots/lab04/29-filter-add-2026.png)

   ![Example comparison with 2026 actuals 26.56M beside Forecast 27.99M](../assets/screenshots/lab04/30-actual-forecast-comparison.png)

   An **example annual comparison (All row, millions to two decimal places)** follows. For 2024 and 2025, the display matches the linked actuals; for 2026, the forecast differs from actuals. Actual values depend on data and settings.

   | Year | Gross Revenue | Forecast |
   |---|---:|---:|
   | 2024 | 24.57 | 24.57 |
   | 2025 | 25.87 | 25.87 |
   | 2026 | **26.56** | **27.99** |

10. Use the arrow on **2026** to expand the year, then expand **Q1** to display January. In the display example, All-row January is **Gross Revenue: 1.92M / Forecast: 2.09M**. Double-click the January **Forecast** cell to read the edit bar, then close with **Escape** without confirming a change.

   ![Example January Forecast edit bar after expanding 2026 and Q1: 2091951.33343](../assets/screenshots/lab04/31-january-forecast-before-close.png)

   Native Gross Revenue is read-only. January actuals appear as a **rounded display such as 1.92M**; this does not provide full precision through an edit bar. The **1,919,542.65** used in the arithmetic reconciliation example below is the cent-precision comparison value from the PBIX data. Forecast display precision likewise does not show every digit of the internally stored value.

   ![Read-only January Gross Revenue displayed rounded to 1.92M, without a full-precision edit bar](../assets/screenshots/lab04/32-january-actual-before-close.png)

<details>
<summary>Breakdown of the original source's 28.01 forecast example</summary>


The original source includes the following example output. Its data or settings differ from the example above, so do not treat these as fixed values.

| Year | Gross Revenue | Original source's Forecast example |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2024 | 24.57 | 24.57 |
| 2025 | 25.87 | 25.87 |
| 2026 | 26.56 | **28.01** |

Growth rates calculated from rounded displays may differ from those calculated at original precision. Align display units, rounding precision, and comparison periods when evaluating percentage changes.

In the original source's example, the statistical forecast is approximately **26.93**, roughly 4.1% above 2025, and a further 4% **Growth Factor** produces **28.01**. This is the original source's output example; results vary by environment.

In other words, the forecast combines “a value derived from history” with “an uplift added by the planner.” Rerunning with Growth Factor set to 0 lets you inspect the statistical forecast alone.

</details>

In the original source's example, January's monthly forecast is approximately **$2.09M** against actuals of **$1.92M**, and the full-year forecast is approximately 5.5% above actuals. You will practice responding to this kind of gap.

lab04-s005.title: Part 4: Close a Period and Extend the Forecast Horizon
lab04-s005.markdown:
January has ended. Close it as an actual period and extend the horizon so the forecast always looks 12 months ahead.

1. Select **Close Period** on the **Model** ribbon. In the **Close Period** dialog, confirm **Select Measure: Forecast**.
2. Set **Close Period till** to **Custom** and open the **Selected Period** date picker. Select **Jan** in 2026 and confirm it shows **Jan 2026**.

   ![Close Period date picker with Forecast and Custom selected, choosing Jan in 2026](../assets/screenshots/lab04/33-close-period-january-picker.png)

3. Turn on **Extend Forecast Range**, set **Duration** to **1 Month**, and select **Preview**.

   ![Forecast, Custom Jan 2026, Extend Forecast Range on, and Duration 1 Month confirmed](../assets/screenshots/lab04/34-close-period-settings.png)

4. In **Confirm Close Period**, check the periods and months to change on the **Forecast** row. An example display follows:

   | Measure | Closed Period | Open Period |
   |---|---|---|
   | Forecast | Jan 2024 - **Jan 2026** | **Feb 2026** - **Jan 2027** |

   ![Example closed period Jan 2024 - Jan 2026 and open period Feb 2026 - Jan 2027](../assets/screenshots/lab04/35-close-period-confirm.png)

   Select **Save** once. Use **Back** to change the settings or **Discard** to cancel. After completion, confirm **Measure updated successfully** appears and January Forecast is replaced by actuals and locked. In the display example, January Forecast is **1.92M** and 2026 All Forecast is **27.82M**.

   ![Example success message after closing, with January Forecast 1.92M and 2026 Forecast 27.82M](../assets/screenshots/lab04/36-close-period-result.png)

   **Reconcile the change in the annual amount.** Double-click 2026 All Forecast, read the edit bar, and close with **Escape**. In the display example it is **27822156.07867**. The following calculation subtracts January's forecast from the previous annual amount and adds January actuals from the PBIX:

   **27,994,564.7621 − 2,091,951.33343 + 1,919,542.65 = 27,822,156.07867**

   ![Example annual edit bar after closing: 27822156.07867](../assets/screenshots/lab04/37-close-period-annual-editor.png)

   When comparing displayed annual values, align the forecast values, actuals for the closed month, and display precision. Matching rounded displays alone does not establish that all detail cells or every digit of internal values match.

The forecast horizon moves forward one month, and January 2026 becomes a closed period. Collapse 2026 and confirm a new **2027 Forecast** year group has been added and is blank. The new open period ends at **Jan 2027**. Next, initialize this added period.

![After extending the horizon, a blank 2027 Forecast year group has been added](../assets/screenshots/lab04/38-extended-2027-blank.png)

Save the entire Plan and verify retention after reloading at the end of step 6. SQL writeback is covered in the next part.

lab04-s006.title: Initialize the New Period
lab04-s006.parent: Part 4: Close a Period and Extend the Forecast Horizon
lab04-s006.markdown:
5. Select **Reforecast Column** on the **Model** ribbon. In the **Reforecast** dialog, target **Forecast** and configure:

   | Setting | Value |
   |---|---|
   | **Target Period** | Jan 2027 - Jan 2027 |
   | **Copy Source** | Gross Revenue |
   | **Apply Operation** | Single Period |
   | **Source Periods** | Jan 2026 |

   Use the calendars to set both the start and end of Target Period to **Jan 2027**, and Source Periods to **Jan 2026**. Before applying, verify that **only the new single month is targeted**, and check the source measure and year.

   ![Example Reforecast settings: Target Jan 2027, Copy Source Gross Revenue, Single Period, Source Period Jan 2026](../assets/screenshots/lab04/39-reforecast-settings.png)

   Select **Apply** once. Confirm **Open periods Re-Forecasted successfully.** appears. In the display example, All in the 2027 group becomes **1.92M**.

   ![Reforecast success message and initial value 1.92M in the 2027 group](../assets/screenshots/lab04/40-reforecast-seeded-result.png)

   Read the edit-bar value and close with **Escape**. The display example is **1919542.65**, the comparison value for January 2026 actuals from the PBIX. **This 2027 column is a year group containing only Jan 2027.** It does not represent individually expanded months or a full 12 months of 2027.

   ![Example 2027 group containing only Jan 2027, with initial edit-bar value 1919542.65](../assets/screenshots/lab04/41-reforecast-seeded-editor.png)

6. Double-click the **All / Forecast** cell in the 2027 group. Without deleting the original **1919542.65**, press **End** to move to the end and append `+4%`. Confirm the expression is **1919542.65+4%** and the input preview is **1,996,324.356**, then press **Enter** once.

   ![Example input appending +4% to original value 1919542.65, with preview 1996324.356](../assets/screenshots/lab04/42-january-2027-plus-four-input.png)

   The display example is **2.00M**. **Saving values** may appear while the value is being applied. This intermediate indicator alone does not mean saving is complete; verify the Plan save and the value after reloading.

   ![Example after appending 4%: 2.00M with Saving values displayed](../assets/screenshots/lab04/43-january-2027-plus-four-result.png)

   Inspect the edit-bar value. The display example is **1996324.36**. Retention after saving is checked by reloading below.

   ![Example edit bar after appending: 1996324.36, to two decimal places](../assets/screenshots/lab04/44-january-2027-plus-four-editor.png)

   | Check | Value | Precision and comparison conditions |
   |---|---:|---|
   | Original edit bar | 1919542.65 | Display example, two decimal places |
   | Independent arithmetic for a 4% increase | 1996324.3560 | Original value × 1.04 |
   | Input preview | 1996324.356 | Display example, three decimal places |
   | Edit bar after appending | 1996324.36 | Matches the expected value rounded to two decimal places |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **1.92M and 2.00M are rounded display values.** Replacing the original edit value with a rounded display does not preserve the calculation's precision. Distinguish input previews, confirmed values, and saved values, and verify the precision used for calculation.

**Save the entire Plan and check values after reloading.** Select **Save** at the top right and wait for saving to finish.

![Example Saving... indicator while saving the entire Plan](../assets/screenshots/lab04/45-rolling-forecast-plan-saving.png)

After saving completes, reload the browser. Open **Forecast** in **Editing** and check that fields, row and column counts, and values are retained. The edit-bar values below are output examples. After reading each cell, close it with **Escape** without confirming a change.

| Target | Example edit bar after reload | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| 2026 All Forecast | **27822156.07867** | Display example |
| 2027 All Forecast (Jan only) | **1996324.36** | Display example |

![Example 2026 Forecast edit bar after reload: 27822156.07867](../assets/screenshots/lab04/46-reloaded-rolling-2026-editor.png)

![Example 2027 group edit bar after reload: 1996324.36, targeting Jan 2027 only](../assets/screenshots/lab04/47-reloaded-rolling-2027-editor.png)

These steps advance the closed month to incorporate actuals, initialize one new month from the same month of the previous year's actuals, apply a 4% adjustment, and save that value within the Plan. The screens in these steps alone do not establish every digit of internally stored values, every detail cell, or SQL writeback.

---

lab04-s007.title: Part 5: Write Back the Data
lab04-s007.markdown:
Save the data created so far within the Plan. Then write it back to Fabric SQL so other features can reference it. Even if an **Add table to semantic model** prompt appears, select **Skip for now** in the main exercise, which covers SQL writeback only. Adding a table to the model is a separately designed operation; do not confuse it with ordinary SQL writeback.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Distinguish the semantic model connection from the SQL writeback destination connection.** Select the existing Fabric SQL connection and database designated for your workshop environment. A connection appearing in the list, access to the model, and the ability to actually write to SQL must each be verified separately.

1. Open the **Writeback** ribbon, switch to **Full View** if needed, and select **Add destination**. In **Create Destination**, select the existing connection and set **Select Database From: Database Item**. Open the OneLake catalog from **Database Name** and select the SQL database designated for the workshop.

   | Setting | Example configuration |
   |---|---|
   | **Select a Connection** | Fabric SQL connection designated for the workshop environment |
   | **Select Database From** | Database Item |
   | **Database Name** | SQL database designated for the workshop environment |
   | **Schema** | dbo |
   | **Table Name** | Forecast |
   | **Decimal Precision** | 2 |
   | **Text Length** | Length of all string columns: 512 |

   Scroll down to check the table name, precision, and string length. **Decimal Precision** may not be changeable after creation, so verify it before adding the destination.

   ![Example Create Destination settings: Forecast, Decimal Precision 2, and Text Length 512](../assets/screenshots/lab04/48-writeback-destination-precision-text.png)

   Select **Add** and confirm **Destination added / Destination ready for writeback** appears.

   ![Example after adding the Fabric SQL Forecast destination; adding it to the model is a separate option](../assets/screenshots/lab04/49-writeback-destination-added.png)

   Writing to SQL and adding a table to the original semantic model are separate operations. If needed, consider adding it to the target model through a separate procedure.

2. Select **Settings** on the **Writeback** ribbon. On the right, under **Writeback Settings → General**, set **Writeback Type** to **Long with Changes**.

   If a **Warning** appears, read it. If it says File / URL destinations do not support this format or changing the format clears selected destinations, reselect the required destination afterward. To continue, select **Proceed** once.

   ![Warning that changing the format clears selected destinations, before finalizing the setting](../assets/screenshots/lab04/50-writeback-format-change-warning.png)

   Confirm **Long with Changes** is selected and **Writeback settings saved successfully** appears. Example settings are **Filter Type: None**, **Decimal Precision: 2**, and **Text Length: 512**. You will reselect the destination in step 4.

   ![Example General settings: Long with Changes, Filter Type None, Decimal Precision 2, and Text Length 512](../assets/screenshots/lab04/51-writeback-general-format-confirmed.png)

> [!TIP]
> There are four formats: Long, Wide, Long with Changes, and Wide with Changes. Long stores one row per cell; Wide stores one column per measure. The with Changes formats handle change history. You will verify the SQL column definitions later. As an advanced exercise, you can separately test the history produced by changing values and writing back again.

3. In the **Data** tab, under **Series allowed for Writeback**, click **the Gross Revenue checkbox itself** to turn it off. Do not assume clicking the label text toggled it; confirm **All: off / Gross Revenue: off / Forecast: on**. Set **Enable Automatic Writeback: off** and confirm the settings-save success message.

   ![Data settings with All and Gross Revenue off, only Forecast on, and automatic writeback off](../assets/screenshots/lab04/52-writeback-only-forecast-checked.png)

4. In **Destinations**, turn on the checkbox for **Fabric SQL / Forecast**. Select the **Forecast** row and confirm it is checked. **Reset Destination** at the bottom is a separate initialization operation.

   ![Forecast selected under Fabric SQL in Destinations, with its checkbox on](../assets/screenshots/lab04/53-writeback-destination-forecast-selected.png)

   Leave **Writeback column rename** in **Advanced** unchanged unless needed. Check filtering under **General → Filter Type** and **Filter** on the ribbon.

   ![Example Advanced Writeback column rename settings](../assets/screenshots/lab04/54-writeback-advanced-settings.png)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Verify permissions for each person executing writeback.** In the current **Security** screen, check **Roles / Users**. Screen settings, the ability to open a sheet, or **Verified** in the model-addition prompt do not by themselves establish writeback permissions. Verify each person's ability to write back through actual execution results and SQL values. Also see the [writeback FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-writeback/writeback-faq).

After reviewing the settings, use **Back to Sheet** to return. Assign participant roles separately according to the workshop environment's permission policy.

![Security screen for reviewing Roles / Users](../assets/screenshots/lab04/55-writeback-current-security-roles.png)

5. Close Settings and select **Writeback** on the **Writeback** ribbon once. If a confirmation dialog appears, read it and continue. Open **Logs** to inspect the result; do not repeat Writeback just to check the outcome.

   Open **Logs** and check writeback status, target scenario, and incoming row count.

   | Item | What to check |
   |---|---|
   | Status | **Success** is displayed |
   | Scenarios | The intended scenario |
   | Incoming Row Count | Input row count appropriate for the targeted data |
   | Writeback Type | The selected writeback format |

   Logs indicate the operation's outcome, but you will reconcile the correctness of values saved in SQL in the next step.

lab04-s008.title: Verify the Values Saved in SQL
lab04-s008.markdown:
6. Open the configured SQL database and use **New Query** to inspect the writeback destination schema. Use the actual table name and schema of the destination selected in your exercise environment.

   ```sql
   SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE, CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH,
          NUMERIC_PRECISION, NUMERIC_SCALE
   FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS
   WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = N'dbo' AND TABLE_NAME = N'Forecast'
   ORDER BY ORDINAL_POSITION;
   ```

7. To inspect current rows, specify **IsLatest = 1** along with the target scenario, measure, and period. The following example is for **Base / Forecast** stored in **dbo.Forecast**. Adapt table names and dimension columns to the actual writeback format.

   ```sql
   SELECT [Year], [Quarter], MonthShort, [Value], IsLatest
   FROM dbo.Forecast
   WHERE IrScenario = N'Base'
     AND ValueColumnName = N'Forecast'
     AND IsLatest = 1
   ORDER BY [Year], [Quarter], MonthShort;
   ```

   To reconcile a particular value with the Plan, select one target leaf cell and record Year, Quarter, Month, Category, SubCategory, scenario, and measure. Check which columns actually exist through `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS`, then include all these keys in the conditions, as in the example below. Replace `<...>` with the values read from the target screen. Do not invent columns absent from the schema; inspect values with read-only SELECT queries.

   ```sql
   SELECT [Year], [Quarter], MonthShort, Category, SubCategory,
          IrScenario, ValueColumnName, [Value], IsLatest
   FROM dbo.Forecast
   WHERE IrScenario = N'<scenario>'
     AND ValueColumnName = N'<measure>'
     AND [Year] = N'<year>'
     AND [Quarter] = N'<quarter>'
     AND MonthShort = N'<month>'
     AND Category = N'<category>'
     AND SubCategory = N'<sub-category>'
     AND IsLatest = 1;
   ```

   Align display units and Decimal Precision between Plan and SQL before comparing, and do not sum mixed grains such as annual totals and monthly rows. `Incoming Row Count` is the input row count for a writeback operation; it does not necessarily match the total row count in the SQL table.

> [!TIP]
> **If the SQL table appears empty**, check log status and incoming row count, then the destination, writeback measures, filters, and scenario in turn. Do not infer persistence to SQL from UI success alone; read current rows in the target table.

> [!WARNING]
> Deleting a row in a planning sheet **does not delete** the row in the writeback destination table. Deleting SQL data requires a database operation. Without agreed owners and operating rules, rows absent from the planning sheet may remain in the table indefinitely.

lab04-s009.title: Save the Writeback Configuration
lab04-s009.markdown: After saving the entire Plan, reopen **Editing → Forecast → Writeback → Settings**. In **General / Data / Destinations**, verify the writeback format, target measures, and destination match your intended settings. Turn **Enable Automatic Writeback** off if you are not using it.

lab04-s010.title: What This Module Covers
lab04-s010.markdown:
This module covers statistical forecast configuration, closing periods, rolling forecasts, initializing and adjusting forecast values, and SQL writeback. Check the historical and target forecast periods, configured scenario, and writeback destination, and reconcile saved values according to their intended use.

**Long with Changes** is a writeback format that handles change history. The log's Incoming Row Count is the input count for that operation and does not necessarily equal the SQL table's total row count. When using destination values downstream, align the period, measure, scenario, and aggregation grain. Deleting rows in the planning sheet does not delete SQL rows.

lab04-s011.title: Verify History and Restoration in a Dedicated Environment (Optional)
lab04-s011.markdown:
For this check, do not use a shared Forecast or business data. Use only a dedicated Plan, SQL database, and destination table designated by the instructor. Limit the exercise to one user and one target cell. Before writeback, read the Plan cell and the complete SQL key and current value. Do not execute SQL that directly modifies the database.

1. Configure **Long with Changes** and verify that writeback is limited to the target scenario and measure. Save the Plan and run **Writeback** once. After checking Logs status, reconcile the latest SQL row and initial value for the same key.
2. Change the target Plan cell, save, and run **Writeback** once. Do not consider the operation complete based only on Logs status. Query the same key in SQL again and check whether the latest and previous values are retained as distinct history. If **PreviousValue / IsLatest** exist, verify their presence in the schema before reading them.
3. Restore the Plan cell to the recorded initial value, save, and run **Writeback** once more. In SQL, confirm the current value for the same key matches the initial value and the previous change is distinguishable as history. Compare the target key with the initial check and confirm no unexpected rows are included.

History columns and row-appending behavior depend on the table and settings. If results differ from expectations, do not keep rerunning; inspect the current SQL value and writeback logs, then consult the instructor. If a dedicated environment is unavailable, skip this optional exercise and do not attempt changes or restoration using shared data.

> [!NOTE]
> **Ordinary SQL writeback and adding a table to the original semantic model are separate operations.** If needed, configure relationships and explicitly select **Apply to model**. Check environment limitations in advance, including support for composite semantic models. See [write planning data back to a semantic model](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-writeback/planning-how-to-write-back-semantic-model).

---

lab04-s012.title: Knowledge Check
lab04-s012.markdown:
1. Why must you apply the year filter before creating the forecast measure?
2. What is the practical difference between **Long** and **Long with Changes**?
3. After closing January, where do actuals come from and where does the planner enter values?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. The statistical model forecasts using history within the target scope. Filtering afterward means the forecast was created using a scope different from the one intended.
2. **Long** replaces rows whose dimension values all match. **Long with Changes** retains previous values as history and writes only changed cells.
3. Closed periods automatically reference actuals from the Gross Revenue measure. Open periods are for data input. Closing a period moves the target month from open to closed.

</details>
